body.statement: There are positive universal constants such that, whenever \(d\geq2\), \(n\) is at least a constant multiple of \(d/\log(ed)\), and \(\log(en)\) is at most a constant multiple of \(\log(ed)\), the minimax mean-squared error for estimating \(\lVert\mathbf P-\mathbf Q\rVert_1\) from two independent samples of respective sizes \(\operatorname{Pois}(2n)\), one from each of \(\mathbf P,\mathbf Q\in\Delta_d\), is bounded below by a positive constant multiple of \(\min\{1,d/[n\log(en)]\}\).

source.locator: Theorem 3, equation (24), and its Poissonized lower-bound proof
source.verbatim_statement: n≥c S/ln S, ln n≤C ln S ⇒ sup_Q inf_L sup_P E_P|L-||P-Q||_1|² ≳_{c,C} S/(n ln n). The lower bound for the known Q case also serves as a lower bound for the unknown Q case.

attestation.note: Verified 2026-09-04 from primary arXiv v7 TeX/HTML source 1705.00807: the paper globally works in the Poisson sampling model; Theorem 3 equation (24) is the displayed worst-Q lower bound, and Section III explicitly transfers the known-Q lower bound to the unknown-Q experiment. The run separately performs the 2n rescaling and fixed-sample transfer.
